# README as Guided Tour

The README is written **for a reader being shown around**, not for a user trying to run something.
Present in all 15 source repositories. Three of them say it in so many words.

## The recurring skeleton

1. Shields.io badges (MIT, "open source · free to use", sometimes stack badges)
2. A centred hero screenshot or figure with a caption
3. An explicit "Start here" line
4. A screenshot table — 2×2, 2×3 or 3-up — each image with a `<sub>` caption saying what to look at
5. An "arc at a glance" table walking the parts in order
6. A fenced repo-layout tree
7. A `## Technology` prose section
8. A `## Skills demonstrated` section
9. `## License`

## Evidence

> "**Start here.** This page is the guided tour of all three projects"
> — Optimization Methods/README.md, 2026-07-10

> "The armory opens for 8 seconds each round… validated server-side, not trusted from the client"
> — browser_game_stickfps/README.md, 2026-07-25

The captions carry argument, not decoration — the second quote is a screenshot caption that explains
[[server-authoritative-netcode]] in passing.

## How far it goes

- `browser_game_stickfps/assets/README.md` documents the **capture settings** for its own
  screenshots: 1600×900 downscaled to 1440 px, progressive JPEG q90, "chosen over PNG to avoid
  banding".
- `Python-Programming-Laboratories/assets/README.md` states provenance: "Real captures, not mockups."
- `Farley` ships **three task-scoped guides** (DEMO / EMULATOR / ANDROID-INSTALL) plus one-click
  `.bat` launchers for each.
- `Information-Systems-Modelling/README.md` runs to **385 lines** with a per-lab chapter each.
- `IT Applications in Business and Commerce` nests **four** guided-tour READMEs.

## Where it is absent

Two repos break the pattern, and they break it the same way — `Oracle-Database-Laboratories` and
`Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories` both have a walkthrough README but **no badges**, and both
bundle README + LICENSE + `.gitignore` into a single final commit rather than the separate polish
commits described in [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]]. Both are also the two most
prose-disciplined repos in the set.

## Reading it critically

A guided tour is a persuasive form, and in several repos the tour is more confident than the code.
`IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/README.md` softens a failure its own sub-README
states flatly ("did not fully solve the S-curve"). `Farley`'s README claims a test suite that does
not exist. The tour is the top of a gradient — see [[documentation-drift]] — and the deeper file is
usually the more honest one, which is itself an instance of
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].
